correctness.summary: For a non-path tree, dim(T)=ell-e and Z(T)=P(T). A maximum matching in the major-vertex induced forest yields a spanning path forest with at most ell-1-nu components, giving Z-dim<=e-1-nu. Konig's theorem then supplies an independent set of at least e-nu exterior major vertices; degree counting gives 3(e-nu)<=n-1. The sharp family and the equality analysis were checked symbolically, and enumeration through order 17 agrees with the formula.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The inspected Eroh-Kang-Yi full text proves dim(T)<=Z(T), records the tree formulas for metric dimension and zero forcing/path cover, and exhibits unbounded-gap families, but no fixed-order maximum was found. The inspected Davila-Henning preprint treats matching and path covers in relation to total forcing, not this order-sharp zero-forcing/metric-dimension gap. Searches of later sparse-graph and path-cover literature did not locate the formula, the matching refinement, or the stated uniqueness theorem.

value.summary: The result gives the exact maximum gap for every tree order, a stronger structural inequality through matching in the major-vertex forest, sharp constructions for every order, and a unique extremal structure for all orders n congruent to 1 modulo 3 with n>=7.

limitations: Unindexed or differently phrased equivalent results remain possible.
The theorem concerns trees and the ordinary zero forcing and metric dimension parameters.
Uniqueness is proved only for n congruent to 1 modulo 3 with n>=7.
